items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer introduces Willie Ruff and his work, and the interviewee responds with 'Yeah.' without adding personal details or confirming a direct relationship.

ctx.x: Get on a boat, he'd get on a ship, you know, and he'd come down to New Orleans, and he'd come back and stay in New Orleans. That's where he learned all his drumming.

Right. That's the way you really do learn it. Willie Ruff. Willie Ruff is a professor, Tootie, at Yale University, and he's a bass player and he's a french horn player and he plays jazz and he plays classical music, and he's brought a big jazz program to Yale, and he says that musicians like you, artists like you, got educated in the conservatory without walls. In other words, in the real world. You heard Henry Kimball, Sr., play. And you heard Nicholson play. And after that, you developed your own style and many…
part of the country, but I did hear Pops play and I did hear Slow Drag play, and Walter Page, and so on.
